newsitem.title: UK: Smiths keeps eye on Thomson's Sextant.
newsitem.headline: Smiths keeps eye on Thomson's Sextant.

text.p: British avionics manufacturer Smiths Industries Plc made it clear on Wednesday that it would be open to offers to partner French firm Sextant Avionique after privatisation of its parent Thomson SA.
The French government announced on Wednesday that it had picked defence to publishing group Lagardere as preferred bidder for Thomson.

Smiths chairman Sir Roger Hurn told a company results news conference on Wednesday in answer to questions that he would be interested in talking to Thomson's new owner if the sale goes ahead, but declined to comment further.
"If the sale goes ahead then we would be interested in talking to the buyer," Hurn said.
He declined to say whether or not Smiths has had specific talks about Sextant's future with Lagardere.
"At the moment we are only an observer of what's going on. We know the people and we have worked with them...This is an industry in which everybody talks to everybody most of the time," he said.

Smith's biggest avionics customer is Boeing Co while Sextant is the main supplier to Boeing's European rival Airbus Industrie. But industry executives say Sextant is in need of a partner to take it outside its home market.
